outcome.evidence: The Board REJECTED the claim: docket entry stamped p3, 'San Francisco Dec. 6 1853 ... Commissioner Thompson Campbell delivered the opinion of the Board rejecting the claim' (opinion stamped pp.35-43, the fatal defect being failure to prove the mesne conveyances from Quijada's heirs, stamped p40). REVERSED on appeal: District Court decree, stamped pp.69-70, 'It is ordered adjudged and decreed that said decision of said Board, Rejecting the claim of the Appellant, be and is hereby Reversed. And further, that the Claim of said Appellant be Confirmed to the lands ceded by the Grant ... Provided that if the Quantity of land within the boundaries set forth by said Petition and Map exceed Eleven square Leagues of land then this Confirmation is for Eleven square Leagues and no more', signed in open court 18 March 1858. Confirmation made FINAL by the United States: Attorney General to U.S. Attorney, stamped p67, 29 September 1856, 'In the case of the claim of Lewis F. Burton, rejected by the Commissioners, case no. three hundred and twelve (312), but confirmed on appeal by the District Court, appeal in the Supreme Court will not be prosecuted by the United States.' Register 'Confirmed' is correct. Patent not in file, but the approved survey is: Surveyor General's certificate, stamped p71, 'the Rancho Bolsa del Chamisal confirmed to L. T. Burton has been surveyed by this office, and ... the survey and plat was approved by the U.S. Surveyor General on the 29 day of June 1861.'

notes: All six fields OK; Hoffman 1862 agrees. TRAP CHECK: this is exactly the 'bare Confirmed hides a Commission rejection' pattern flagged in the method - the Board rejected on 6 Dec 1853 and the District Court reversed - but here the reversal IS in this single volume (no multi-volume note), so the outcome is settled, not guessed. Two internal snags a re-reader should not be misled by: (1) the District Judge's DRAFT opinion, stamped p79, misstates the grant as 'from Governor Alvarado to one Francisco Quintana bearing date 11 of March 1837' - both the surname and the month are wrong against the Spanish original at stamped pp.17-18 and against the Board's own recital at stamped p35; the draft is heavily struck through. (2) the AG's 1856 letter already speaks of a District Court confirmation while the decree in the file is dated 18 March 1858, so an earlier decree preceded this one; either way the direction of the outcome is unambiguous. The grant was contested at the Mexican end too: Canuto Guevara petitioned for the same paraje and the Santa Barbara ayuntamiento preferred Quijada because he had cattle and horses to stock it while 'Canuto is not known to have any property' (translation of expediente, stamped p14). An adverse claim is visible in the record and is worth flagging for the ranchos register: Abel Stearns testified before the Board (stamped pp.5-6) that 'A part of this land is covered by a title to Catalina Ruiz ... The whole of this land is included in her title while I have same. The claim is under an old grant to Manuel Nieto' - i.e. the Bolsa Chica overlapped Nieto's Los Alamitos/Los Coyotes. name.evidence: The file itself carries at least five forms and none is exactly the register's. outcome.evidence: Board CONFIRMED: opinion of Commissioner Thompson Campbell, stamped p23, 'We are therefore of opinion that the claim in this case should be confirmed'; decree of confirmation stamped p24, signed Alpheus Felch, Thompson Campbell, R. Aug. Thompson, filed 20 Dec 1853. District Court AFFIRMED: decree stamped pp.48-49, filed 24 Sept 1855, 'it is ordered, adjudged and decreed that the said decision be in all things affirmed ... that the claim of appellee to a certain tract of land known by the name of Bolsa de Escarpines is valid ... corrections.name: 'Bolsa de los Escarpines' is the form in every Spanish leaf (expediente cover stamped p10; petition stamped p11); the register's 'Bolsa De Las Escorpinas' follows Hoffman's printed table, not the case file

notes: Year, governor, land_case, outcome OK; name and grantee PART on form only. Hoffman 1862 agrees on substance. SUBSTANTIVE POINT for the register: the 7 Oct 1837 Alvarado act is NOT a fresh concession but a CONFIRMATORY decree replacing lost papers - its own words (translation, stamped p16) are that Espinosa 'has occupied quietly & peaceably for the space of fourteen years the land ... with the knowledge of the ancient Governors of California, the documentary proofs of which he shows have been mislaid in the proper office.' That puts the original cession at roughly 1823, in Luis Antonio Arguello's governorship, and the neighbouring Natividad possession is dated to 1823 'by the Order of the then Governor of California Don Luis Antonio Arguello' at stamped p58. The Board understood it exactly this way (stamped p23: 'The party had not only obtained a title from the Spanish Government, but he had occupied without interruption for the space of fourteen years the same land'), and the U.S. Attorney's ground VII was that the 1837 paper 'is not a grant' at all (stamped p36). The register's era tag 'alvarado' and year 1837 are therefore right about the operative title but hide an earlier Arguello-era origin. Also of note: the Board found 'no proof that any approval was ever made by the departmental Assembly' (stamped p23) and confirmed anyway, on equitable grounds (District Court opinion, stamped p47, invoking 'the principles of Equity made by the Act of 3 March 1851'). Espinosa died before 1868; his heirs petitioned the District Court to correct a boundary mistake in the 1855 decree (stamped pp.54-62). The first called "El Moro Cojo" stated to contain about two square leagues of land was granted for the purpose of placing his cattle thereon to said deceased by Governor Arguello on the 14th of February 1825, under whose order he was put into possession on the 9th day of March following.' The claimants' petition, stamped p4, and the U.S. Attorney's own petition for review, stamped p90, both say the same: 'A portion of said tract was granted in the year 1825 to said Don Simeon Castro by Dn Luis Arguello then Governor of the Territory of Upper California and juridical possession thereof given.'

governor.evidence: All four names in the register are attested, in the register's order. Board opinion, stamped p78: first grant 'by Governor Arguello on the 14th of February 1825'; 'The second grant bears date May 14th 1836 & is signed by Governor Mariano Chico. This grant covers a portion of the premises claimed a little more than one square league in extent and known by the name of "Bolsa Nueva"'; 'The third grant was made by Governor Alvarado on the 20th day of November 1837'; and stamped p79, 'On the 25th day of September 1844 Governor Michelterena made a grant in accordance with this petition, and caused it to be delivered together with the previous grants to the widow.' The Chico decree is in the file in Spanish, stamped p21: 'Monterey 14 de Mayo de 1836 ... se declaro al S. Simeon Castro dueño en propriedad del terreno conocido con el nombre de Bolsa Nueva en aumento del que ya posee llamado Bolsa del Moro Cojo ... El S. D. Mariano Chico Gefe Politico de este Departamento de la Alta California asi lo mando, decreto y firmo. Mar.o Chico.'

grantee.evidence: Chico decree, stamped p21: 'se declaro al S. Simeon Castro dueño en propriedad del terreno conocido con el nombre de Bolsa Nueva'; Alvarado's order of 11 June 1840, stamped p22, 'librese testimonio de ella a la parte de D. Simeon Castro en confirmacion del terreno de Bolsa Nueva que obtuvo en 14 de Mayo de 1836 ... Alvarado'; Board opinion, stamped p78, 'granted ... to said deceased by Governor Arguello'. Maria Antonia Pico de Castro (widow) and the eight Castro children are the U.S.-era CLAIMANTS (p1 red label, petition stamped p4), and the register correctly holds the Mexican grantee Simeon Castro instead.

Containing Eight Square leagues of land more or less', signed Alpheus Felch, Thompson Campbell, R. Aug. Thompson. The United States appealed and fought hard (AG Cushing's notice, stamped pp.85/87, 17 Jan 1855; Pacificus Ord's petition for review, stamped pp.89-101, filed 24 Aug 1855, alleging in grounds VI-VIII that the Alvarado paper 'is not a grant in fee ... informal, vague, indefinite, and void ... fraudulent', that the Micheltorena decree 'was never approved by the Departmental Assembly of California, or the Supreme Executive of Mexico', and that two maps in the expediente copy 'did not form part of, and belong to the original Expediente No. 164, at the time they purport to have been made - And they are fraudulent'). notes: All six fields OK - and this is the most complicated register entry in the chunk, a four-governor composite that the register gets right. Hoffman 1862 agrees, and Hoffman's own long governor string is simply the Board's three-grant chain. Chain as the Board found it (opinion, stamped pp.78-79): (1) El Moro Cojo, ~2 sq leagues, Arguello, 14 Feb 1825, possession 9 Mar 1825; (2) Bolsa Nueva, ~1 sq league, Mariano Chico, 14 May 1836, after Francisco Maria Soto renounced the tract Arguello had conceded HIM in Dec 1824 (Soto's renunciation, stamped p16, 'el terreno llamado La Bolsa Nueva concedido por el S.D. Luis Arguello en el año de 1824 lo renuncio y lo pone a disposicion del Gobierno'; Soto's own 1824 petition and Arguello's marginal decree of 20 Dec 1824 are at stamped p15); (3) the intervening land, Alvarado, 20 Nov 1837; then (4) Micheltorena's confirmatory grant of the whole eight leagues, September 1844, on the widow's petition. ONE INTERNAL CONFLICT a re-reader should know about: Simeon Castro's OWN petition of 27 April 1836, stamped p14, dates the Moro Cojo concession to 1829, not 1825 - 'el terreno llamado Bolsa del Mozo cojo que tiene concedido en el año de 1829 por el Sor Gobernador D. Luis Arguello' - which is anachronistic on its face (Arguello left the governorship in 1825) and is contradicted by the Board's finding, by the claimants' 1852 petition and by the U.S. Attorney's petition; the register's 1825 stands. The register's era tag 'echeandia' is odd given a 1825 Arguello grant, but there IS an Echeandia document in the file (stamped p77, 'Prov.y Lt.e S. Diego 13 de Junio de 1829, Jose Ma de Echeandia', a note about delivering title papers to Jose Joaquin de la Torre and 'el Cabo Simeon Castro'), which may be where that tag came from. The Micheltorena date wanders across the file - 25 Sept 1844 (Board opinion, stamped p79), 16 Sept 1844 (Board decree, stamped p82), 24 Sept 1844 (Ord's petition, stamped p90), 26 Sept 1844 (District Court decree, stamped p110) - and the underlying petition of Maria Antonia Pico is dated 14 Sept 1844 in one place and 11 Sept 1844 in another; none of this touches a graded field. notes: Five fields OK, grantee PART on abbreviation only; Hoffman 1862 agrees. SUBSTANTIVE POINT for the register, same pattern as Bolsa de las Escorpinas in this chunk: Alvarado's 30 Sept 1837 act is a CONFIRMATORY decree replacing lost papers, not an original concession. Rodriguez's own petition, stamped p16 and in translation at stamped p23, says the place was granted to him by 'el finado D. Luis Argüello' with possession given by the retired lieutenant Don Jose Estrada 'el año veinte y tres' (1823), and that his papers were lost 'el año veinte y siete cuando el Sor Echandia recojio los papeles de los sitios' - i.e. destroyed in Echeandia's 1827 recall of rancho titles. The alcalde's possession act of 3 Nov 1837, stamped p21, gives possession 'sin las formalidades acostumbradas, por tenerlas echas en el año de 1823.' The Board accepted this reading (stamped p30: 'The Petition in this case states that in the Year 1823 he obtained a grant to the place in question from Governor Luis Arguello and that said grant was lost'). So the register's 1837/Alvarado is right about the operative title but conceals an 1823 Arguello origin, and the register's era tag would be better read as Arguello-with-Alvarado-confirmation. Two harmless slips inside the file: the Board opinion's caption, stamped p30, places the rancho 'in the County of Santa Clara' while its own decree two pages later says Santa Cruz; and the claimant's petition is bound twice (rough hand at stamped pp.4-6, fair copy at stamped pp.36-37), the fair copy being much the easier read. year.evidence: Grant decree (Doc. No. 1, Spanish original), stamped p18: 'Dado en la ciudad de los Angeles en papel comun por falta del sellado à ocho de Julio de mil ochocientos cuarenta y cinco. Pio Pico. Josè M.a Covarrubias, Sec.no.' Sworn translation, stamped p15: 'Given in the city of Los Angeles on this common paper for want of stamped, one in the 8th of July 1845.' Board opinion, stamped p32: 'By grant from the Mexican Government issued by Governor Pio Pico to one Felipe a Neophyte Indian of the Mission of San Luis Rey which bears date the 8th day of July AD 1845.' governor.evidence: Grant decree, stamped p17: 'Pio Pico Gobernador interino del departamento de las Californias'; signed 'Pio Pico' with 'Josè M.a Covarrubias, Secretario', stamped p18. Santiago E. Arguello, who knew both men, swore to the signatures: deposition, stamped p6, 'a grant from Governor Pio Pico to Felippe an Indian of the mission of San Luis Rey bearing date the eighth day of July A.D. 1845 and I recognise the signatures of Pio Pico and Jose Maria Covarrubias appearing thereon to be their true and genuine signatures.'

grantee.evidence: The grantee really is a single given name, and the register is right to record it that way. Felipe's own petition, stamped p9, is signed simply 'Felipe' and opens 'Felipe indigena de la mision de San Luis Rey'; translation stamped p14, 'I Felipe a native of the Mission of San Luis Rey ... being possessed of a small piece of Land called Buenavista belonging to the Mission of San Luis Rey since the year 1836 ... I believe to be entitled to it because being a native of this mission where I have labored so much'; grant decree, stamped p17, 'Por cuanto Felipe natural de la Mision de S.n Luis Rey ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno conocido con el nombre de Buenavista'; the mission administrator's informe, stamped p9, calls him 'el Indigena Felipe'. outcome.evidence: Board CONFIRMED: opinion of Commissioner Thompson Campbell, stamped p32, 'The evidence documentary and oral filed in this cause establish beyond all question the right of the Petitioner to a confirmation of the land claimed ... we are therefore of opinion that the same should be confirmed'; decree stamped p33, signed Felch, Campbell and Thompson, filed 16 May 1854, 'the Claim of the said Petitioner is valid and it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed ... containing in all one half of a Square League.' The United States appealed; the District Court AFFIRMED at Los Angeles on 1 Feb 1856 before Judge Ogier ('the opinion of the Court was delivered confirming the claim of the Appellee herein', minute recited at stamped p93); the U.S. then took an appeal to the Supreme Court (order 7 March 1856, stamped p99) and ABANDONED it (Attorney General Cushing to P. Ord, stamped p88, 4 October 1856, 'In the case of the claim of Jesus Machado, confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, case no. six hundred and eighteen (618), and also confirmed on appeal by the District Court, appeal will not be prosecuted by the United States', filed 24 Feb 1857). Register 'Confirmed' is correct.

notes: All six fields OK; Hoffman 1862 agrees, including his bare 'Felipe' for the grantee. TWO THINGS WORTH CARRYING INTO THE REGISTER. (1) This is a grant to a mission INDIAN in his own name - Felipe, a Luiseno neophyte of San Luis Rey, who petitioned on his own behalf and signed with his single name; the mission administrator Jose Joaquin Ortega supported him because 'he has rendered in his youth and part of his old age all his services to the same [mission] without this administration knowing that at any time he has given occasion to blame' (translation, stamped p14). Half a square league only. He sold out within five years (to William B. Dunn, then jointly to Jesus Machado, deeds recited in the petition at stamped p4 and the Board opinion at stamped p32), which is the ordinary post-1848 fate of the few Indian grants and is exactly the kind of case the register should not lose behind the claimant's name. (2) The register's very late patent date (1897) is explained inside the file: although the District Court confirmed on 1 Feb 1856, 'owing to misprision or neglect no decree was ever signed by any Judge of the said last mentioned Court' (stamped pp.95-96), so no decree existed to patent on. The defect was cured only 23 years later by a NUNC PRO TUNC decree of Ogden Hoffman, 14 April 1879 (stamped pp.90-97), 'Ordered, adjudged and decreed that the said decision be and the same is hereby in all things affirmed as of the date of the First day of February 1856 ... and that the said claim be and the same is hereby confirmed to the extent of One half of a square league of land a little more or less', entered after the Southern District and its court were abolished by the Act of 27 July 1866 and the cause transferred. Por cuanto Ramona Sanchez ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno conocido con el nombre del Butano ... he venido en concederle el mencionado paraje con estencion de un sitio de ganado mayor entendiendose dicha concecion provicional y sujetandose à la Aprovacion ó desaprobacion de la Exma Diputacion. notes: Five fields OK, grantee PART on the given-name spelling; Hoffman 1862 carries no year/governor/grantee for this rancho at all, so the register's data here is BETTER than Hoffman and is fully borne out by the case file. Two points worth keeping. (1) The register's parenthetical 'ratified by Micheltorena' is unusually exact: the 1844 instrument is literally headed a 'revalidacion' of the 1838 provisional title (stamped p21), and Micheltorena's one-word marginal order is 'Revalidase' (stamped p18). The revalidation was applied for not by Ramona herself but by her eldest son Jose Antonio Galindo, 'having attained majority and been emancipated', in her name (petition, Monterey 8 Nov 1844, stamped p18, translation stamped p24). (2) The original title papers were LOST IN THE MAIL during the claim: John H. Watson, the claimant's first attorney, deposed that he posted the original grant to Clark, Taylor & Beckh at San Francisco and it never arrived (stamped pp.8-9, and Gustavus W. Beckh's corroboration recited at stamped p32), so the Board confirmed on secondary evidence, expressly saying the proof 'is not so full and satisfactory as could be desired' and 'exceedingly loose and unsatisfactory' but sufficient given the archive expediente (stamped pp.32-33). Note also that the same expediente cover, stamped p16, carries a SECOND heading, 'Espediente Promovido por Ramona Sanchez en pretencion del paraje llamado Bolsa del Butano' - a related but distinct paraje that a re-reader should not conflate with this claim. name.evidence: Spanish expediente cover, stamped p12: 'Espediente promovido por D.a M.a Ygnacia Lopez en solicitud del parage conocido con el Nombre de "Cabeza de Santa Rosa". 255'; grant, stamped p18, 'el parage conocido con el Nombre de Cabeza de Sta Rosa'; p1 red label 'PART OF CABEZA DE SANTA ROSA GRANT'. NOTE the qualifier: this docket covers only PART of the rancho (transcript title, stamped p1, reads 'for the place named Part of "Cabeza de Santa Rosa"', the word 'Part of' inserted by hand), namely the portion north of the Arroyo de Santa Rosa. The rancho NAME is right; the register should not be read as saying ND 124 covers the whole grant.

year.evidence: Grant (Exhibit A, Spanish original), stamped p19: 'Dado en Monterey à treinta de Sep.tbre de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y uno. Manuel Jimeno. Josè D. Fernandez Srio in 1o.' The concession decree in the expediente carries the same date, translation stamped p17: 'Monterey Sept. 30, 1841. Having seen the petition with which this Espediente begins, the report of the Commanding Genl and everything else presented and proper to be seen, in conformity to the Laws and regulations upon the subject I declare Dna. Maria Ygnacia Lopez owner in property of the place known by the name of "Cabeza de Santa Rosa".' Registered in the Prefectura of the 1st District 5 Oct 1841 (stamped p19).

governor.evidence: The grant is Jimeno's, made as acting governor, and the file says so in its own words: grant, stamped p18, 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin 1er vocal propietario de la Ex.ma Junta Departament.l en ejercicio del Gobierno del mismo'; translation of the concession, stamped p17, 'Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin first vocal presiding over the Departmental Junta Exercising the Office of Governor, thus Ordered decreed & signed as I certify. Jimeno.' Jimeno's power to grant while Alvarado held the commission was THE contested question in the case and the Board upheld it after a long review of the law of 23 June 1813, the decree of 6 May 1822, the act of 1837 art. 20 and the Bases Organicas of 1843 (opinion, stamped pp.45-51): 'It is only in the event of the absence of the Governor from the Capitol that Jimeno was authorized to make grants of the public domain ... I am therefore of opinion that prima facie proof of authority in Jimeno to exercise the powers which he assumed when he made the grant in question has been established and the grant is valid and in conformity with Law' (stamped pp.48-49). Mariano G. Vallejo swore to Jimeno's and Jose D. Fernandez's signatures (deposition, stamped p10).

grantee.evidence: Grant, stamped p18: 'Por cuanto D.a Maria Ignacia Lopez ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el parage conocido con el Nombre de Cabeza de Sta Rosa'; translation, stamped p17, 'I declare Dna. Maria Ygnacia Lopez owner in property of the place known by the name of "Cabeza de Santa Rosa"' - the register's spelling matches the sworn translation exactly. Her own 1838 petition, stamped p13 (translation stamped p16), is signed for her by her son: 'Sonoma 19th Juny 1838. At the request of my Mother, Joaqn Carrillo.' Julio Carrillo is the U.S.-era CLAIMANT (p1 red label), one of her ten children, to whom the other heirs conveyed the north portion after partition; the register correctly holds the Mexican grantee instead. Claimant's abstract, stamped p95: 'The grantee was the widow of Joaquin Carrillo (Salvador Vallejo p.2). She died in 1850 or 1851 leaving ten children.'

land_case.evidence: p1 red label 'CASE NO. 124 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; leaf 2 'Land Case 124 ND, 97 pages'; every leaf stamped '124 ND'; printed District Court decree caption, stamped p84, 'IN LAND CASES. District Court No. 124'; caption stamped p86 'District Court No 124 / Land Commr No 643 / Part of "Cabeza de Santa Rosa"'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_nd124.pdf. Board (Commission) docket no. was 643, exactly Hoffman's commission_no.

outcome.evidence: Board CONFIRMED: opinion of Commissioner Thompson Campbell, stamped pp.45-51, 'For these reasons we are of opinion that the claimant is entitled to a confirmation of that part of the Rancho called "Cabeza de Santa Rosa" described in his petition to this Commission, and a decree of confirmation will accordingly be entered'; decree, stamped p52, 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the said petitioner is valid and it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed ... That portion of the above described premises of which confirmation is hereby made to the said petitioner is all that portion of the above place Cabeza de Santa Rosa which lies on the North side of the Arroyo de Santa Rosa in the County of Sonoma', signed Felch, Campbell and Thompson, filed 4 April 1854. The United States appealed (claimant's abstract, stamped p95: 'The Board Confirmed the Claim ... and the United States appealed. The Claimant asks that the decree of the Board be affirmed'), and the appeal failed: by 1860 the case had reached the SURVEY stage, which only a FINAL confirmation reaches. Order on return of monition, stamped p84, District Court, Ogden Hoffman, 24 October 1860, 'proclamation was made that all parties having, or claiming to have, an interest in the survey and location of the land FINALLY CONFIRMED in the above entitled cause, appear and intervene'; and the decree confirming survey, stamped pp.88-89, filed 3 January 1861, 'It is thereupon adjudged, ordered, and decreed, that the approved survey heretofore made by the United States Surveyor General for California, of the lands confirmed to the claimant, in the above entitled cause ... be and the same is in all things hereby confirmed and ratified. Ogden Hoffman, Dist Judge.' Register 'Confirmed' is correct; the 1861 survey decree also explains the register's 1866 patent date. No patent copy in the file.

notes: All six fields OK; Hoffman 1862 agrees (his 'Maria Ygnaeia Lopez' is an OCR/typesetting artefact of Ygnacia). ONE STRUCTURAL POINT the register must not lose: the Cabeza de Santa Rosa grant was carved up among SIX separate land cases, and this docket is only one of them. Claimant's abstract, stamped p95, in Crittenden's hand: 'This Claim and Nos 125, 126, 127, 128 & 235, are all under the same grant, and there is no controversy between the several claimants. Their claims cover the whole grant', with the further note 'By stipulation on file the deposition of Alvarado taken in 124 is considered as taken in each of these cases.' So ND 124 = Julio Carrillo's share north of the Arroyo de Santa Rosa (register's 4,500.42 acres, roughly one of the two granted leagues), and ND 125-128 and ND 235 hold the rest. Chain as the abstract states it (stamped pp.93-95): Maria Ygnacia Lopez petitioned Comandante General M. G. Vallejo 19 Jan 1838 and he let her settle pending adjudication (his marginal order, translation stamped p16, 'Sonoma Juny 24th 1838. The petitioner may settle on the land she asks with the understanding, that she shall solicit from the Political Govt the title of adjudication of property'); second petition to the Governor 1 June 1840; Jimeno's concession and title 30 Sept 1841 for two sitios de ganado mayor; juridical possession by Salvador Vallejo January 1842. Salvador Vallejo testified he gave the possession himself as civil magistrate of Sonoma and that 'the Monuments are there' still (stamped pp.6-7); Mariano G. Vallejo testified she 'had an excellent dwelling house upon it, and dwelt there cultivating the ground and raising stock upon it PRIOR to the grant' (stamped p10).
